responseText: {"title":"Two Sides of a Face","question":"How does a face hold together when its two sides differ?","introduction":"Every face here is split: one eye open, one crossed out; one socket a spiral, one a flat disc; one cheek warm, one cold. These thirty works arrange themselves around that basic asymmetry, moving from faces where the difference is subtle to ones where the two halves seem to belong to entirely separate systems. Look at what holds them together — and what doesn't.","closing":"Each face here stays in one piece despite the visible pull between its two sides. Whether that tension reads as unease, alertness, or something else is left open by the works themselves.","chapters":[{"title":"One Eye Open, One Eye Not","introduction":"These faces announce their asymmetry through a single sharp contrast: one eye rendered with care, the other crossed out, cancelled, or simply absent. The split is immediate and frontal.","stops":[{"slot":"W002","whyHere":"The wide concentric left eye and the crossed-out right socket establish the exhibition's central problem in its bluntest form.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W067","whyHere":"A bold red X cancels the right cheek while the left eye socket remains intact — cancellation made into a structural element rather than a mark.","transitionFromPrevious":"W002 crosses out an eye with hatched marks; W067 replaces that gesture with a hard red X, making the erasure larger and more architectural."},{"slot":"W090","whyHere":"A yellow cross on the left and a red slash on the right give each eye zone a different symbol of negation, doubling the cancellation across the face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W067 uses one X on one side; W090 assigns a different cancellation mark to each eye, so neither side escapes."},{"slot":"W129","whyHere":"One socket is open and petal-ringed; the other is sealed by a red X — the same crossed-out logic, now set against a face that contains a smaller face inside it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W090 cancels both eyes with flat symbols; W129 restores one eye to full openness, making the X on the other side feel like a deliberate choice rather than a system."}]},{"title":"Spiral Against Flat","introduction":"Here the asymmetry shifts from cancellation to construction: one eye is built from coiling lines, the other from a flat fill, a grid, or a simple disc. The two marks refuse to agree on how an eye should be made.","stops":[{"slot":"W221","whyHere":"A wide blue-white spiral on the left faces a compact red-orange rosette on the right — two entirely different mark systems occupying the same face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W129 pairs an open petal eye with a crossed one; W221 replaces the X with a dense rosette, so both sides are now active but still incompatible."},{"slot":"W085","whyHere":"A dark inward spiral on the left and a wide outlined eye on the right pull attention in opposite directions across a yellow-gold face.","transitionFromPrevious":"W221 keeps both eyes compact; W085 stretches the contrast — one eye collapses inward, the other opens wide into a drawn outline."},{"slot":"W112","whyHere":"The left side is buried under layered scribble where an eye might be; the right opens into a tight spiral aimed at a red dot — the most extreme version of this buried-versus-revealed contrast.","transitionFromPrevious":"W085 gives each eye a legible form; W112 removes legibility from the left side entirely, replacing it with accumulated mark-making."},{"slot":"W199","whyHere":"One eye is a deep wound of spiral lines; the other is a flat crosshatched shape — the spiral-versus-flat contrast pushed to its most compressed, urgent form.","transitionFromPrevious":"W112 buries one side under scribble; W199 replaces that scribble with a tight crossed shape, making the contrast between the two sides feel more locked and confrontational."},{"slot":"W200","whyHere":"A coiled spiral on the left and a crosshatched rectangle on the right sit at different heights, giving the face a stacked, off-balance structure built from two incompatible geometries.","transitionFromPrevious":"W199 keeps both eye zones close together; W200 places them at different heights, so the asymmetry becomes spatial as well as formal."},{"slot":"W142","whyHere":"A golden disc eye and a concentric teal loop refuse to mirror each other; red bars slice the brow above them, adding a mechanical band to the organic asymmetry below.","transitionFromPrevious":"W200 uses warm amber to unify its mismatched eyes; W142 introduces a cool grey-green ground and a hard red bar, making the split feel more structural and less organic."}]},{"title":"Faces Under Pressure","introduction":"These works add a third element: the background or surrounding field presses inward, and the face must hold its asymmetry against that external force. The split inside the face and the pressure from outside work on each other.","stops":[{"slot":"W040","whyHere":"A tightly wound right eye and a loose scrawled left eye sit inside a head that the striped background pushes against with equal visual weight.","transitionFromPrevious":"W142 has a flat, contained ground; W040 surrounds its mismatched eyes with diagonal stripes that press in from every edge."},{"slot":"W034","whyHere":"Radiating blue lines converge from all sides onto a face whose two eyes are ringed in different colors; the background's agitation and the face's asymmetry reinforce each other.","transitionFromPrevious":"W040's background stripes run parallel; W034's lines radiate inward, so the pressure feels directed at the face rather than surrounding it."},{"slot":"W088","whyHere":"A black mask holds a red spiral and a blue spiral — mismatched by color — while crossed bands of yellow, grey, and red pack the surrounding field with equal density.","transitionFromPrevious":"W034's background radiates outward from the face; W088's field is horizontal bands that neither radiate nor recede, pressing the mask flat against them."},{"slot":"W058","whyHere":"Two spiral forms — one tight, one loose — sit above a red bar and a stepped white border; the rigid geometry of the surround presses against the organic asymmetry of the eye pair.","transitionFromPrevious":"W088's background is all-over bands; W058 introduces a hard geometric border on one side only, so the pressure is asymmetric too."},{"slot":"W022","whyHere":"A skull with one layered socket and one flat fill sits inside a dense tangle of looping lines that press close to its outline on all sides, making the external pressure visible as a surrounding mass.","transitionFromPrevious":"W058's border is a single edge; W022's line tangle surrounds the skull completely, closing off every gap between the form and its field."},{"slot":"W071","whyHere":"A dark spiked circle holds a crossed blue eye and a green rectangle eye; yellow loops crowd the background without resolving, keeping the surrounding space as restless as the face inside it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W022's surrounding tangle is dense and uniform; W071's background loops are looser and more scattered, so the pressure feels less like a wall and more like noise."}]},{"title":"Ceremony and Alarm","introduction":"Several faces add crowns, halos, decorative borders, or radiating marks that frame the asymmetric eyes in something ceremonial. The ornament does not resolve the split — it frames it.","stops":[{"slot":"W152","whyHere":"A spiked crown rises above two mismatched spiral eyes; the ceremonial headpiece and the off-balance eyes sit in the same image without one explaining the other.","transitionFromPrevious":"W071's crown is made of jagged points that read as alarm; W152's crown is more elaborate, adding gold and purple, so the ceremonial quality is stronger even as the asymmetry below it persists."},{"slot":"W031","whyHere":"A flat-topped hat caps a face split between yellow and cold teal, with two mismatched eyes below it; hands at the edges add a further ceremonial or greeting gesture.","transitionFromPrevious":"W152's crown rises from the head; W031's hat sits flat on top, a different kind of headgear that reads as costume rather than crown."},{"slot":"W117","whyHere":"A skull form wears yellow-gold scalloped rings around each socket — decorative borders that frame the asymmetry rather than hiding it, against a dark ground with diagonal color bands.","transitionFromPrevious":"W031's hat is a flat structural cap; W117's scalloped rings are applied to the eye sockets themselves, so the ornament is closer to the asymmetry it frames."},{"slot":"W189","whyHere":"A circular form ringed by grey-tipped ovals and radiating yellow marks frames two mismatched eye forms — one daisy-ringed, one a spiral target — inside a halo of outward-pointing shapes.","transitionFromPrevious":"W117's decorative rings are tight to the sockets; W189's radiating marks extend far beyond the face, making the ceremonial frame the dominant visual fact."},{"slot":"W138","whyHere":"Jagged yellow borders around each mismatched socket echo the zigzag teeth below; the ornamental borders link the eye asymmetry to the mouth, pulling the whole face into a single decorative system that still doesn't resolve the split.","transitionFromPrevious":"W189's radiating marks push outward; W138's jagged borders stay close to the face, tightening the ornament back around the features."}]},{"title":"The Face as Assembled Object","introduction":"The final group treats the face less as a body part than as a constructed thing — color patches that don't follow outlines, features locked in separate frames, or a face containing another face. Asymmetry here is a condition of assembly, not a flaw.","stops":[{"slot":"W075","whyHere":"Each feature is locked inside its own framed zone — sun-circle eye, spiral eye, boxed mouth — as though the face were a cabinet of separate compartments that happen to share a boundary.","transitionFromPrevious":"W138's face is unified by its decorative system; W075 breaks the face into discrete framed zones, so the asymmetry becomes structural rather than ornamental."},{"slot":"W083","whyHere":"Two mismatched orange eyes burn above a gridded mouth that reads as both grin and cage; striped limbs dangle at the edges, giving the face a puppet-like, assembled quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W075's compartments are tightly framed; W083's limbs extend beyond the body, so the assembled quality spills outside the face's boundary."},{"slot":"W173","whyHere":"A flat pink outline holds a tight red spiral and a sun-ring eye; a coiled white rod extends from the mouth, adding a mechanical component that sits alongside the organic marks as an equal part of the assembly.","transitionFromPrevious":"W083's extra parts are limbs; W173's extra part is a mechanical rod at the mouth, shifting the assembled quality from puppet to something more wired and strange."},{"slot":"W143","whyHere":"Color patches float free of the drawn outlines, so the face reads as two overlapping systems — one drawn, one painted — that share a space without fully merging; the oversized left eye and smaller right eye make the mismatch visible at the level of drawing itself.","transitionFromPrevious":"W173's assembly is additive, with parts attached; W143's assembly is layered, with drawn and painted systems occupying the same space independently."},{"slot":"W160","whyHere":"A tight white spiral and a looping pink flower mark two eye zones inside a large outlined form; wave lines pile up inside and outside the boundary, so the face and its field are made from the same marks and the assembled quality extends to the whole canvas.","transitionFromPrevious":"W143's two systems stay within the face; W160's marks spill beyond the outline, dissolving the boundary between the assembled face and the space around it."},{"slot":"W181","whyHere":"A coiling spiral on the left and a jagged triangular tangle on the right are built from opposite geometries; the face pushes to the frame edges, and the bared teeth below read as the one fixed point in an otherwise unresolved assembly.","transitionFromPrevious":"W160's boundary dissolves into its field; W181 reasserts a strong outer edge while keeping the interior split between two incompatible geometries, closing the exhibition on a face that holds together by pressure alone."},{"slot":"W012","whyHere":"Dense scribble lines pile up differently around each eye — one heavily shadowed, one sitting higher with a pale surround — while surrounding color bursts feel raw and unresolved, an honest contrast to the more structured assemblies preceding it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W181 holds its form through a strong outer edge; W012 has no such containment — the face pushes to the picture edge and the surrounding marks feel unfinished, ending the gallery on a note of open, unresolved asymmetry."}]}]}
